question: A person on anti-tubercular drugs complained of deafness and tinnitus in one ear. Drug implicated is?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ethambutol" -> "optic neuritis" -> "visual disturbances" -> "no direct link to deafness" -> 30%
analysis: The core medical principle here involves understanding the side effects associated with anti-tubercular drugs. Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used in the treatment of tuberculosis and is well-documented to cause ototoxicity, which can manifest as deafness and tinnitus. This is due to its effect on the auditory nerve and inner ear structures. In contrast, isoniazid is more commonly associated with peripheral neuropathy, ethambutol with optic neuritis, and rifampicin with hepatotoxicity. Given the symptoms of deafness and tinnitus, streptomycin is the most likely drug implicated. This aligns with the enhanced information provided, which supports the consensus that streptomycin is linked to these auditory symptoms.
